I've been farming this land since I was a little girl helping my parents, and now I manage our 10.1 mu here in Quzhou. With six mouths to feed and some family working off-farm, I need to be smart but not wasteful. We have well water, so I can irrigate when the sky doesn't give us enough, but every time I start the pump it costs money, so I only water when the crops are truly thirsty.

My wheat is already in the field from last autumn. I planted improved seed because it grows strong and doesn't fall over easily. Now that spring is here, I will topdress with urea when the wheat turns green and irrigate right after. I'll water again at the jointing stage and once more when the grain is filling if the rain holds back. For chemicals, I'll spray twice—once for weeds and once for insects or disease if I see them in the field. I won't till the wheat ground again; that would kill the crop.

After we harvest the wheat in early June, there's no time to rest. I'll rotary-till the stubble quickly and plant hybrid maize seed the same day or the next—hybrid maize is the only choice now, the old types don't give enough grain. I'll put compound fertilizer in the furrows at planting, then add urea when the corn reaches knee height. The maize will need one or two irrigations, and I'll spray twice for weeds and corn borers. I know this land well, and if the weather is fair, my wheat should give me about 500 kg per mu and the maize about 600 kg per mu.
